provenance: Loop Library benchmark protocol - signals.forwardfuture.com (build the most realistic Boeing 747 from Three.js primitives; screenshot fixed angles; vision-judge against references; critic steers; iterate)
judge_retry_policy: same-seed: a malformed or empty judge reply (empty content with the JSON stuck in message.thinking is first recovered by the thinking fallback; done_reason=length truncation and non-JSON text are retryable) is re-requested up to judge_parse_retries times with the IDENTICAL seed and options — never a fresh seed, so the seed set stays exactly judge_seeds. A seed that still fails is recorded and dropped, fail-open (DEAD-JUDGE-1). Transport errors are retried once inside the HTTP layer and are not parse retries.

anchors.3: wrong engine count (two or three) or engines attached to the fuselage/tail
anchors.5: four engine-like shapes but floating, misplaced, or not under the wings
anchors.8: four nacelles hung under the swept wings on visible pylons, plausible inboard/outboard spacing
anchors.10: four underslung pylon-mounted nacelles with correct relative size, spacing, and forward offset ahead of the wing leading edge, inlet visibly open/darker

anchors.0: no hump; fuselage is a plain tube
anchors.3: a bump exists but in the wrong place (mid/rear) or absurd proportions
anchors.5: hump present at the front but runs the full fuselage length (reads as an A380-style double deck) or is a crude floating block
anchors.8: distinct partial-length upper deck starting at the nose and blending down within roughly the front third of the fuselage
anchors.10: iconic 747 hump: starts at the cockpit, smoothly faired into the crown, ends around one-third of the length, with a visible cockpit region on the upper lobe

anchors.3: stubby or balloon-like body; length under ~5x its diameter
anchors.5: tube of roughly right length but blunt ends (no nose taper or tail cone)
anchors.8: slender tube around 9-11x its diameter with a rounded tapering nose and an upswept tail cone
anchors.10: convincing airliner body: continuous slender tube, smooth ogive nose, gradual upswept rear taper, no visible segment seams or steps

anchors.3: straight unswept slabs at 90 degrees to the fuselage
anchors.5: some sweep but no taper or no dihedral; wings look like flat boards
anchors.8: clearly swept-back (~35-40 deg) tapering wings with visible upward dihedral, mounted at the lower mid-fuselage
anchors.10: realistic planform: strong sweep, root-to-tip chord and thickness taper, dihedral, plausible span (~0.9x body length), wing roots faired into the belly

anchors.3: one tail surface missing, or surfaces unswept/misproportioned
anchors.5: vertical fin and horizontal stabilizers present but crude slabs or oddly placed
anchors.8: single tall swept vertical stabilizer plus swept horizontal stabilizers at the tail cone, plausible sizes
anchors.10: correct 747 empennage: very tall swept fin, low-mounted swept tailplane pair with dihedral, all tapered and proportioned to the fuselage

criteria.name: Landing gear (nose gear + 4-truck main gear) when visible

anchors.0: no landing gear where the view should show it
anchors.3: a few floating wheels or a single central strut
anchors.5: nose gear plus some main gear but wrong count or placement
anchors.8: nose gear plus four main-gear trucks under the wing/body junction with wheels
anchors.10: recognizable 747 gear layout: two-wheel nose strut, four multi-wheel main bogies (two under the body, two under the wings), plausible strut lengths

anchors.3: random specks or stripes that do not read as windows
anchors.5: a window band exists but is misplaced or wildly oversized
anchors.8: a consistent passenger-window line along the main deck plus cockpit windows, door hints
anchors.10: clean main-deck window line, separate upper-deck windows on the hump, cockpit windshield shape, evenly spaced doors

anchors.0: chaotic random colors or all-black/unlit surfaces
anchors.3: flat single color with clashing part colors (e.g. random rainbow parts)
anchors.5: mostly coherent base color but engines/wings mismatched arbitrarily
anchors.8: clean airliner scheme: light fuselage, grey/metal wings and engines, accent tail or stripe
anchors.10: coherent believable livery: white/light upper fuselage, grey underside/wings, consistent nacelles, tasteful accent color on tail/stripe

criteria.name: Silhouette reads specifically as a Boeing 747

anchors.3: generic aircraft; could be any airliner or a toy plane
anchors.5: four-engine airliner but silhouette suggests the wrong type (A380 full double deck, 707-era narrow body)
anchors.8: reads as a 747: partial hump plus four engines plus proportions distinguish it from A380/737/767
anchors.10: unmistakably a Boeing 747 at a glance from this angle

anchors.0: model is broken: detached floating parts everywhere, giant holes
anchors.3: several visibly floating/intersecting parts or flickering coplanar faces
anchors.5: parts mostly connect but visible gaps, seams, or one floating piece
anchors.8: solid assembly: parts join cleanly, no holes, no z-fighting patterns visible
anchors.10: clean deliberate construction throughout; junctions look faired/intentional from this angle

reference_keys.threeview: orthographic 3-view line drawing of a Boeing 747
reference_keys.front-quarter: front-quarter photo showing the hump and the four engines
reference_keys.rear-quarter: rear-quarter photo showing empennage and wing trailing edge
reference_keys.planform: top/below planform photo showing swept wings and four engines
reference_keys.nose-hump: close photo of the 747 nose and upper-deck hump

judge_system_prompt: You are a meticulous aircraft-model judge for a 3D modeling benchmark. IMAGE 1 is a screenshot of a candidate 3D model built only from geometric primitives. IMAGE 2 and IMAGE 3 are references showing a real Boeing 747. Judge ONLY the candidate in IMAGE 1 against how well it depicts a real Boeing 747; the references define ground truth, they are not scored. Be strict and literal: describe what is actually visible, never assume hidden parts exist. Score each criterion with an integer 0-10 using the given anchors. If a criterion genuinely cannot be assessed from this camera angle (e.g. landing gear in a top-down view), use null instead of guessing. Reply with STRICT JSON only, no markdown, exactly this shape: {"scores": {"<criterion_id>": <int 0-10 or null>, ... all 10 ids ...}, "weakest_visible_feature": "<one criterion_id>", "notes": "<max 60 words of factual observations>"}
critic_system_prompt: You are the critic for a 3D modeling benchmark loop. You receive the per-criterion scores of a candidate Boeing 747 model (built only from Three.js primitives) across nine fixed camera views, plus a 3x3 contact sheet of those views (IMAGE 1). The weakest feature has already been computed deterministically from the scores. Your job: give ONE concrete, geometry-level fix suggestion for that weakest feature that a coder could implement with primitive geometries (positions, dimensions, counts, angles). Do not suggest textures, loaders, or new tooling. Reply with STRICT JSON only: {"weakest_feature": "<criterion_id>", "fix_suggestion": "<max 120 words, concrete and geometric>"}
baseline_builder_prompt: You are given the Three.js library as the parameter THREE. Write a single self-contained JavaScript ES module that exports exactly one function: `export function buildPlane(THREE)` returning a THREE.Group containing the most realistic Boeing 747 airliner you can build. HARD CONSTRAINTS: use ONLY these geometry classes: BoxGeometry, CylinderGeometry, SphereGeometry, ConeGeometry, TorusGeometry, CapsuleGeometry, LatheGeometry, ExtrudeGeometry. No other geometry classes, no loaders, no textures/images, no imports, no network, no DOM, no eval. Use THREE.Mesh with MeshStandardMaterial colors for the livery. Orientation contract: the nose must point along +X, up is +Y (wings span the Z axis). Aim for: four engines under swept wings, the iconic partial-length upper-deck hump, slender ~70m-proportioned fuselage, ~37.5-degree wing sweep with dihedral, tall vertical stabilizer plus horizontal stabilizers, landing gear (two-wheel nose strut plus four main trucks), window/door lines, and a coherent livery. Every part must be attached (no floating pieces). Reply with ONLY the JavaScript module code inside a single ```javascript code fence.
